const arr = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5];

// Transform
arr.map(x => x * 2)             // [2,4,6,8,10]
arr.flatMap(x => [x, x*2])      // [1,2,2,4,3,6,...]
arr.filter(x => x % 2 === 0)    // [2,4]
arr.reduce((acc,x) => acc+x, 0) // 15

arr.every(x => x > 0)           // true

// Sort (MUTATES!)
[...arr].sort((a,b) => b-a)     // [5,4,3,2,1] — copy first!
['b','a','c'].sort()             // ['a','b','c']

// Flat
[[1,2],[3,[4]]].flat()          // [1,2,3,[4]]
[[1,2],[3,[4]]].flat(Infinity)  // [1,2,3,4]

// Convert
Array.from({length:5}, (_,i) => i)  // [0,1,2,3,4]

customCards.title: Key Concepts
customCards.note:
HEAD      — pointer to the current commit / branch tip
Index     — the staging area (what will go into next commit)
Working tree — your actual files on disk

Three-tree architecture:
  Working Tree  --(git add)-->  Index  --(git commit)-->  .git repo

Detached HEAD — HEAD points to a commit instead of a branch.
               Create a branch to save your work: git checkout -b new-branch

Fast-forward merge — moves branch pointer forward; no new commit created.
3-way merge        — creates a merge commit when histories have diverged.

Origin   — conventional name for the default remote (GitHub/GitLab/etc).
Upstream — the branch your local branch tracks on the remote.

def greet(name: str, greeting: str = 'Hello') -> str:
    return f'{greeting}, {name}!'

# *args and **kwargs

# Lambda

# Decorator
from functools import wraps

def log_call(func):
    @wraps(func)
    def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
        print(f'Calling {func.__name__}')
        result = func(*args, **kwargs)
        print(f'{func.__name__} returned {result}')
        return result
    return wrapper

@log_call
def add(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return a + b

# Closure
def make_counter(start=0):
    count = start
    def increment():
        nonlocal count
        count += 1
        return count
    return increment

counter = make_counter()
print(counter())  # 1
print(counter())  # 2

# try / except / else / finally
try:
    result = int('not a number')
except ValueError as e:
    print(f'Conversion error: {e}')
except (TypeError, OverflowError):
    print('Type or overflow problem')
else:
    print('Runs only when NO exception was raised')
finally:
    print('Always runs — use for cleanup')

# Custom exception
class InsufficientFundsError(ValueError):
    def __init__(self, amount: float, balance: float):
        super().__init__(f'Need {amount:.2f}, only have {balance:.2f}')
        self.amount = amount
        self.balance = balance

# Context manager (with statement)
with open('file.txt', 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    content = f.read()  # file closes automatically

# Custom context manager via contextlib
from contextlib import contextmanager

@contextmanager
def temp_directory():
    import tempfile, shutil
    path = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    try:
        yield path          # code inside 'with' block runs here
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(path) # cleanup regardless of exceptions

with temp_directory() as tmp:
    print(f'Working in {tmp}')

customCards.title: Async / Await
customCards.code:
import asyncio
import aiohttp

# Basic coroutine
async def fetch_json(url: str) -> dict:
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
        async with session.get(url) as resp:
            resp.raise_for_status()
            return await resp.json()

# Run concurrently — both requests happen at the same time
async def main():
    urls = [
        'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users',
        'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts',
    ]
    users, posts = await asyncio.gather(*[fetch_json(u) for u in urls])
    print(f'{len(users)} users, {len(posts)} posts')

# Timeout
async def with_timeout():
    try:
        async with asyncio.timeout(5.0):
            return await fetch_json('https://slow-api.example.com')
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        return None

# Async generator
async def paginate(base_url: str):
    page = 1
    while True:
        data = await fetch_json(f'{base_url}?page={page}')
        if not data:
            break
        yield data
        page += 1

if __name__ == '__main__':
    asyncio.run(main())

customCards.title: LangChain — Basic Chain with Memory
customCards.code:
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from langchain_core.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate, MessagesPlaceholder
from langchain_core.output_parsers import StrOutputParser
from langchain_core.runnables.history import RunnableWithMessageHistory
from langchain_community.chat_message_histories import ChatMessageHistory

# 1. Model
llm = ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4o-mini', temperature=0)

# 2. Prompt with history placeholder
prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_messages([
    ('system', 'You are a helpful assistant.'),
    MessagesPlaceholder(variable_name='history'),
    ('human', '{input}'),
])

# 3. Chain via LCEL pipe
chain = prompt | llm | StrOutputParser()

# 4. In-memory session store
store: dict = {}
def get_session(session_id: str) -> ChatMessageHistory:
    if session_id not in store:
        store[session_id] = ChatMessageHistory()
    return store[session_id]

# 5. Wrap chain with history management
with_history = RunnableWithMessageHistory(
    chain,
    get_session,
    input_messages_key='input',
    history_messages_key='history',
)

# 6. Invoke — session_id keeps conversations separate
config = {'configurable': {'session_id': 'user-123'}}
response = with_history.invoke({'input': 'What is LangChain?'}, config=config)
print(response)

# 7. Second turn — history is automatically included
response2 = with_history.invoke({'input': 'Give me a code example'}, config=config)
print(response2)

customCards.title: LangChain — RAG Pipeline
customCards.code:
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI, OpenAIEmbeddings
from langchain_community.vectorstores import Chroma
from langchain_community.document_loaders import TextLoader, DirectoryLoader
from langchain.text_splitter import RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
from langchain_core.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate
from langchain_core.runnables import RunnablePassthrough
from langchain_core.output_parsers import StrOutputParser

# 1. Load documents
loader = DirectoryLoader('./docs', glob='**/*.txt', loader_cls=TextLoader)
docs = loader.load()

# 2. Split into chunks
splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(
    chunk_size=500,
    chunk_overlap=50,    # 10% overlap prevents context loss at boundaries
)
chunks = splitter.split_documents(docs)

# 3. Embed and store in vector DB
embeddings   = OpenAIEmbeddings(model='text-embedding-3-small')
vectorstore  = Chroma.from_documents(chunks, embeddings, persist_directory='./db')
retriever    = vectorstore.as_retriever(search_kwargs={'k': 4})

# 4. RAG prompt
prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_template("""
Answer the question based only on the following context.
If the answer is not in the context, say 'I don't know'.

Context:
{context}

Question: {question}
""")

# 5. Build RAG chain
llm = ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4o-mini')

def format_docs(docs):
    return '\n\n'.join(d.page_content for d in docs)

rag_chain = (
    {'context': retriever | format_docs, 'question': RunnablePassthrough()}
    | prompt
    | llm
    | StrOutputParser()
)

# 6. Query
answer = rag_chain.invoke('What are the key features?')
print(answer)

customCards.title: LangGraph — Stateful Agent
customCards.code:
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, END
from langgraph.prebuilt import ToolNode
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage
from langchain_core.tools import tool
from typing import TypedDict, Annotated
import operator

# 1. State — messages accumulate via operator.add
class AgentState(TypedDict):
    messages: Annotated[list, operator.add]

# 2. Define tools
@tool
def web_search(query: str) -> str:
    """Search the web for current information."""
    return f'Search results for: {query}'  # replace with real API

@tool
def calculator(expression: str) -> str:
    """Evaluate a safe math expression like '2 ** 32'."""
    allowed = set('0123456789+-*/(). ')
    if not set(expression).issubset(allowed):
        return 'Invalid expression'
    return str(eval(expression))

tools = [web_search, calculator]

# 3. LLM bound to tools
llm = ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4o', temperature=0).bind_tools(tools)

# 4. Nodes
def agent_node(state: AgentState) -> dict:
    response = llm.invoke(state['messages'])
    return {'messages': [response]}

tool_node = ToolNode(tools)  # handles tool execution automatically

# 5. Routing — continue to tools or end
def should_continue(state: AgentState) -> str:
    last = state['messages'][-1]
    return 'tools' if (hasattr(last, 'tool_calls') and last.tool_calls) else END

# 6. Build and compile graph
graph = StateGraph(AgentState)
graph.add_node('agent', agent_node)
graph.add_node('tools', tool_node)
graph.set_entry_point('agent')
graph.add_conditional_edges('agent', should_continue)
graph.add_edge('tools', 'agent')  # loop back after tool use
app = graph.compile()

# 7. Run
result = app.invoke({'messages': [HumanMessage('What is 2 to the power of 32?')]})
print(result['messages'][-1].content)

customCards.title: Tool Calling & Pydantic Schemas
customCards.code:
from langchain_core.tools import tool
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from typing import Optional

# Method 1: @tool with docstring (LLM reads the docstring to decide when to call)
@tool
def get_weather(location: str, unit: str = 'celsius') -> str:
    """Get current weather for a location.

    Args:
        location: City and country, e.g. 'Paris, France'
        unit: Temperature unit — 'celsius' or 'fahrenheit'
    """
    return f'Weather in {location}: 22 {unit[0].upper()}, Sunny'

# Method 2: Pydantic input schema (more control, better validation)
class SearchInput(BaseModel):
    query:       str            = Field(description='The search query')
    max_results: int            = Field(default=5, ge=1, le=20)
    site:        Optional[str]  = Field(default=None, description='Limit to domain')

@tool('web_search', args_schema=SearchInput)
def web_search(query: str, max_results: int = 5, site: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
    """Search the web for information."""
    q = f'site:{site} {query}' if site else query
    return f'Top {max_results} results for: {q}'

# Bind tools to model and invoke
tools = [get_weather, web_search]
llm = ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4o').bind_tools(tools)

response = llm.invoke([HumanMessage('What is the weather in Tokyo?')])
for call in response.tool_calls:
    print(f'Tool: {call["name"]}, Args: {call["args"]}')

customCards.title: Design Patterns & Best Practices
customCards.note:
AGENT PATTERNS
ReAct — Reason + Act: LLM reasons what to do, calls a tool, observes result, repeats.
Plan-and-Execute — Planner generates steps; Executor runs each. Good for long tasks.
Reflection — Agent critiques its own output and revises. Improves quality.
Multi-agent — Orchestrator delegates to specialist sub-agents.

RAG TIPS
• chunk_size 300–800 works for most text; smaller for code/tables
• chunk_overlap 10–15% prevents context loss at chunk boundaries
• Re-rank retrieved chunks with a cross-encoder before inserting into context
• Hybrid search (keyword + semantic) beats pure semantic for exact queries

TOOL DESIGN RULES
• One tool = one clear action. Keep scope narrow.
• Write detailed docstrings — the LLM reads them to decide WHEN to call.
• Always return strings or JSON-serialisable values.
• Validate inputs with Pydantic; raise clear, descriptive errors.

COST CONTROL
• Use gpt-4o-mini / claude-haiku for routing/classification tasks.
• Cache identical calls: from langchain.globals import set_llm_cache
• Count tokens before sending with tiktoken.
• Stream responses to reduce perceived latency.

SAFETY
• Never put API keys in code — use .env + python-dotenv.
• Add guardrails on tool inputs; never pass raw user input to eval() or shell.
• Set max_iterations on AgentExecutor to prevent infinite loops.
• Log all tool calls and LLM inputs/outputs for debugging and audit.
